clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old man with chronic kidney disease who underwent heart transplantation 3 months prior presented with a 3-week history of right thigh pain followed by acute onset of fever (38°C), chills, and tachycardia (HR 130). Physical examination revealed a new grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border (tricuspid regurgitation), right thigh tenderness, and right lung base findings (dullness and decreased breath sounds). Initial workup demonstrated Gram-positive bacilli on blood Gram stain. Transoesophageal echocardiography revealed a small mobile mass on the tricuspid valve consistent with vegetation. Blood cultures returned positive for Nocardia asteroides. Imaging confirmed disseminated infection: MRI of the right proximal leg showed a 2×1.5×3 cm abscess within the right vastus lateralis muscle; CT chest revealed multiple peripheral lung nodules with right-sided pleural effusion; and brain MRI demonstrated a 9 mm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe. Antimicrobial therapy was initiated with oral trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX) based on Gram stain findings, and imipenem–cilastatin was added upon confirmation of CNS involvement. The patient improved with treatment, with resolution of the brain abscess on follow-up MRI and stable tricuspid regurgitation on repeat echocardiography, with no evidence of residual infection.
